MEDICARE BASICS

Start with the essentials.

Medicare is federal health insurance for people 65 and older and some people under 65 with qualifying conditions.

Parts A and B

Original Medicare includes Part A (hospital insurance) and Part B (medical insurance). It generally does not cover every cost or most routine dental care, so many people compare additional coverage options.

MEDICARE SUPPLEMENT · MEDIGAP

A little help with the gaps.

Medigap policies work alongside Original Medicare and may help pay certain deductibles, copayments, or coinsurance. Benefits are standardized by plan letter, while premiums and availability vary.

Medigap does not include prescription drug coverage. You can compare Part D separately.

MEDICARE ADVANTAGE · PART C

Understand how the plan works.

Medicare Advantage plans are offered by private companies approved by Medicare and provide your Part A and Part B coverage. Many include drug coverage and extra benefits.

Compare provider networks, costs, plan rules, and whether your prescriptions are covered.

PRESCRIPTION DRUG COVERAGE

Check your prescriptions.

Part D helps cover prescription medicines. Plans can differ in premiums, formularies, pharmacies, and out-of-pocket costs.

Make a current list of your medicines and preferred pharmacy before comparing options.

DENTAL COVERAGE

Look closely at the details.

Original Medicare generally does not cover routine dental care. Some Medicare Advantage plans include dental benefits, and standalone coverage may also be available.

Check covered services, provider access, waiting periods, and annual limits.

ENROLLMENT TIMING

Know the dates that matter.

Your enrollment windows depend on your situation and the type of coverage you are reviewing.

Annual Enrollment Period

Each year, Oct 15 through Dec 7 is the Annual Enrollment Period for people with Medicare to review and make certain changes to Medicare Advantage or Part D coverage for the following year.

Initial enrollment and other special enrollment periods follow different rules. Confirm the dates that apply to you before making a change.
